commitResults.messageTitle: Extract console interaction into Ui class
commitResults.messageBody: Move standard-input command reading and console output behind Ui so Bogos can focus on application flow. Keep command text and formatting unchanged to preserve the existing console interface while establishing a clear boundary for later Storage, Parser, and TaskList extractions.

Move Bogos banner, divider, indentation, and farewell text into Ui. Replace generic output calls with named UI operations so Bogos coordinates commands without owning console formatting or fixed presentation strings.

Move task-file loading, record validation, deserialization, and saving from Bogos into Storage. Bogos now coordinates when persistence occurs, while Storage owns the data-file details and preserves existing recovery messages through Ui.

Move task storage, one-based lookup validation, addition, and deletion from Bogos into TaskList. Also pass a Path to Storage using Paths.get so the data-file location is constructed without a hard-coded path separator.

Move task-command interpretation, field validation, date parsing, event validation, and task-number parsing from Bogos into Parser. Bogos now dispatches commands and coordinates the parsed data with TaskList, Storage, and Ui.
Organize into Packages
Add JUnit Tests

Java classes use abbreviated field names and have inconsistent formatting and public-method documentation.

Rename ambiguous fields and accessors, add required documentation, and apply consistent whitespace so the code follows the project Java standard.

The project needs a shared reference for applying the SE-EDU Java conventions to production code and tests.

Add the Java coding-standard skill and require it before Java changes so future work follows the same rules.

Future commits need consistent messages and branch names that make project history easier to review.

Add the Git-standard skill and require it before branch and commit work.
Let users find tasks by a case-insensitive keyword in their descriptions.\n\nCover matching results in unit and console UI tests.

commitResults.messageBody:
Java assertions are not used to document internal assumptions or detect
unexpected state changes during development.

Adding assertions at internal method boundaries and after state-changing
operations makes violated invariants fail fast without replacing user-input
validation.

Let's add assertions for command routing, task state transitions, and
task-list removal.

Loading the data file combines file iteration, record parsing,
completion-state restoration, and malformed-record reporting.

Keeping file iteration focused on reading records and collecting valid
tasks improves readability.

Let's move record parsing, completion-state restoration, and malformed-
record reporting into a dedicated helper.

Bogos.processCommand mixes command dispatch, persistence, error
handling, and UI-response construction.

This makes the command-processing flow harder to read and mixes levels
of abstraction.

Let's separate command dispatch and list-response construction from the
method that coordinates execution, saving, and error handling.

Deadline and Event define the same user-facing date formatter.

Duplicated formatting rules can diverge and produce inconsistent task
displays.

Let's define the formatter in Task so date-bearing task types share one
presentation rule.

MainWindow declares an injected sendButton field that no code reads.

The FXML already binds the button action to handleUserInput, so the
unused field makes readers look for a dependency that does not exist.

Let's remove the unused field and its import.

Task command prefixes are duplicated in Bogos and Parser.

Duplicated classifications can cause a command to be accepted in one
location but rejected in another.

Let's make Parser own task-command prefix definitions and use its
classification when Bogos dispatches commands.

Console and graphical command handling use separate expressions to
recognize the exit command.

Duplicated command checks can diverge when the exit syntax changes.

Let's use Bogos's exit-command predicate in the console loop so both
interfaces share the same decision.

Task types are represented by single-letter strings throughout task
construction and storage loading.

Raw strings allow unsupported types and make the meaning of each
code implicit.

Let's represent the supported task types with a TaskType enum while
retaining their existing data-file codes.

The enum makes valid task types explicit without changing the
persisted format.

Storage parsing accesses fields and field counts by raw numbers.

These values obscure the data-file schema and invite incorrect indexes.

Let's name each field position and expected record size.

The constants explain the schema at each use without changing file
compatibility.

Deadline and event parsing repeats marker strings for lookup and
offset calculations.

Repeated marker literals can become inconsistent when command formats
change.

Let's define each date marker once and use it throughout parsing.

The constants keep position calculations aligned with marker
recognition.
Add Java assertions
Improve code quality

The chat view stops responding to mouse-wheel scrolling after a user
sends a command.

Users cannot review earlier messages without first dragging the scroll
bar, which makes navigation through the conversation unreliable.

Let's update the chat view so that it follows new messages without
disabling mouse-wheel scrolling.

This keeps the latest response visible while allowing users to revisit
earlier messages at any time.
Restore mouse-wheel scrolling

Tasks do not allow tagging.

Tags make it easier to identify related tasks.

Let's allow tags when creating tasks, retain them across sessions,
and reject blank or duplicate tags. Existing task records remain
untagged.

Bogos uses the default JavaFX appearance, which does not reflect his
playful alien persona.

Give the chat interface a retro-alien palette and a branded header.
Differentiate user and Bogos messages so conversation history is easier
to scan.

Keep command-processing behavior unchanged while making the app's visual
identity match Bogos.

Task commands treat a repeated date parameter as part of a date value,
which produces a misleading format error. Duplicate-error messages also
use wording that does not match the Bogos voice.

Let the parser reject repeated /by, /from, and /to parameters before
reading their values. Use "buplicate" in all duplicate user messages
and cover the errors in unit and console UI tests.

This gives users a targeted explanation and keeps parser behavior
documented at both test levels.

New dialogs can be laid out after the queued scroll operation runs. The
view then remains above the latest response even though a message has been
sent.

The scroll value must stay writable so users can review earlier messages
with the mouse wheel or scroll bar.

Let's trigger auto-scrolling when the dialog container height changes. Those
changes occur after layout reflects the new dialog, keeping the latest
response visible without binding the scroll value.
Fix chat auto-scroll timing

Event commands accept start and end dates that are equal. Commands with
surrounding or repeated whitespace are handled inconsistently, and
identical tasks can be added more than once.

These cases produce ambiguous task data or force users to match command
formatting exactly.

Let's reject events that do not end after they start, normalize command
whitespace, and prevent duplicate task details. Document the rules and
cover them with unit and console UI tests.

The User Guide explains whitespace normalization and duplicate detection
in implementation-level terms.

That detail distracts from the rules users need when entering commands.

Let's describe duplicate-task rejection in plain language and omit the
forgiving whitespace behavior.
Improve task input validation
